problem: The final accountant review stopped at the first revised approval: Check status and reload retained Confirmation needed with no current approval recorded and controls locked (AC-R3-001). The recovery text repeated a long unbroken signature, widening the 390 px page to 653 px (AC-R3-002), and described an approval uncertainty as a payment issue (AC-R3-003). Browser evidence establishes these symptoms, not the transaction outcome. Parent separately reports that the exact submitted approval signature is confirmed; that source-aware network finding must be independently bound to the saved operation before any application reconciliation.
userImpact: The accountant cannot finish a payable despite having an apparent recovery control, cannot explain which person's action is uncertain, and encounters horizontal overflow precisely when help is needed. The payable must remain unpaid and protected while uncertainty persists, but a read-only check should be able to recognize an already confirmed matching approval without asking the user to submit again.
proposedChange: The user authorized two more iterations if needed; propose this as recovery cycle 3, subject to PM/SDE acceptance. Make Check status perform bounded, read-only reconciliation of the saved transaction and operation. It may promote the already recorded pending operation into authoritative application state only when chain evidence proves successful confirmation and exact binding to the saved scenario, action, actor, obligation, revision and expected business change. This is idempotent local reconciliation, never signing, rebroadcasting or issuing a replacement transaction. Keep failed, unseen, unconfirmed, ambiguous and mismatched outcomes blocked with a useful last-check result. Show action-specific recovery copy, such as Mara Weber's approval of 800 Test USD is awaiting confirmation; this approval does not move funds. Display checking progress, last check and result, then refresh the approval count only after verified reconciliation. Put a single transaction identifier in a labeled technical disclosure/copy field with wrapping. In Evidence, show an explicitly unresolved operation section separate from completed events; replace it with the actual confirmed record only after safe reconciliation. Scope is recovery state/contract, read-only reconciliation and its UI; no payment/credit/approval resubmission or ledger-authority changes.
acceptanceCriteria: The user has authorized two more iterations if needed under the existing shared budget. This proposal is recovery cycle 3; implementation waits for PM/SDE acceptance. Cycle 4 is not automatically started by this proposal.

A saved, exactly bound approval transaction that chain evidence proves successfully confirmed is reconciled once into the current application approval record by Check status. Repeated checks and page reload produce the same record and count; no new signature, wallet signing, transaction submission, RPC send or duplicate approval event occurs.

The verifier uses durable pre-submission operation identity and expected transition, not a pasted signature, message substring or a generic success status alone. Missing/mismatched actor, scenario, obligation, revision, program/action or expected result leaves state blocked. SDE must specify the exact available evidence and matching rules before implementation; unsupported recovery must be disclosed rather than inferred.

Unknown, failed, unseen, unconfirmed, rate-limited and otherwise ambiguous outcomes remain protected. A failed or unavailable status read does not clear the operation lock, change payable balances, record an approval as confirmed, or enable payment. The interface reports that confirmation was not established and offers another safe status check without a retry-payment or retry-approval control.

Recovery names the actual operation, actor and amount from saved metadata. An approval recovery explicitly says approval does not move funds and never claims a payment was sent or failed. Credit and payment uncertainties use their own accurate language; generic fallback says operation when type-specific identity is unavailable.

Check status has a visible checking state, prevents overlapping checks, and reports its latest result and timestamp. Continued uncertainty explains that the payable remains locked until its outcome can be verified. No schedule, infinite polling or unsupported escalation button is introduced.

At desktop and 390 px, error/status banners, payment rail and the identifier disclosure fit the viewport without horizontal overflow. Raw identifiers wrap or truncate with an accessible full-value disclosure; repeated long signatures are removed from ordinary guidance. Copy controls operate on the actual identifier only.

Evidence distinguishes the pending operation from immutable completed records and never presents it as a confirmed approval or payment. Existing invoice, credit, approval and payment records, archived evidence and protected ledger remain unchanged except the one verified pending transition becoming its actual recorded result. No fabricated receipt or chain outcome is allowed.

Run typecheck/build and targeted integration tests proving exact confirmed reconciliation, repeat-check idempotency, mismatch rejection and failed/unseen/unconfirmed/rate-limit lock retention. A fresh-context browser regression checks action-specific recovery and no overflow at both widths. Separate source-aware network evidence from accountant usability evidence, and do not require an extra payment or reset solely to test layout.
tradeoffs: A meaningful status check requires a small explicit reconciliation contract and durable pending-operation metadata; this exceeds a cosmetic copy fix and therefore needs engineering review despite the newly granted user authorization.

The parent is already reducing redundant transport reads under existing core integration scope. That fix may prevent recurrence but does not replace this proposal's persisted-unknown recovery behavior or authorize its implementation.
Conservative unresolved states may remain blocked even after a known failed transaction. This bounded proposal does not introduce resubmission, reset-to-unlock, manual override or cancellation paths.

An unresolved-operation section helps accounting explanation but is not a completed ledger event. It must remain visibly distinct from confirmed evidence and must not rewrite original exported records.

Human-readable export formats and broader visual/accessibility redesign remain deferred. Fresh-context browser review remains instructionally isolated, not technically isolated or proof of production accounting fitness.
